name: Bear
tagline: ASCENT does not land: no contracts beyond today's demand, reliability stalls
rationale: Only today's flown demand (RQ1/RQ2) without the shift away from rideshare, no paid readiness contract, the ESA Launcher Challenge ends in 2030 without a successor, Nova Scotia is not taken up, success stays at the 75 % the insurance market prices

name: ASCENT (base)
tagline: Our strategy executed: contracts first, Nova Scotia only with an anchor
rationale: Visible demand plus two frame-contract launches a year from 2029 (A), paid readiness at 15 % growth (S), Nova Scotia opened with 3 anchor launches a year (T), a successor programme keeps half of the ESA level after 2030, success rises to 92 % by 2030 as in RQ2

name: Bull
tagline: Sovereign demand surges: Europe buys readiness and launches at scale
rationale: European space-security budgets turn into contracts: readiness grows 25 %, six frame-contract launches a year from 2029, six anchor launches at Nova Scotia, hypersonic test flights in blocks, the ESA level continues after 2030, success 95 %
